title: Command-line utilities without installing anything on the machine

videos.script: A container does not have to be a server. It can be a tool that runs for one command and disappears. {{pattern}} The pattern is one line: remove the container afterwards, mount the current folder, start there. With it, Ana reads a YAML file, finds a bug in a shell script, and six problems in a Dockerfile, with none of those tools installed. {{versions}} The version is in the tag, so two versions are two tags. One Python script works on three point thirteen and fails on three point twelve, side by side. {{wrapper}} A small shell function makes the tool feel installed, and one flag makes the files it writes belong to you. {{limits}} Then the limits. A file one folder up does not exist. Every call costs a third of a second. And credentials have to be handed in, so you had better trust the image.
